rows.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
rows.subtopic: Periodic Trends in Properties of Elements
rows.text: Which one of the following statements best describes the acidic/basic/amphoteric nature of \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) and \(\mathrm{CaO}\)?

Which among the following processes is/are associated with increasing bond order but no change in diamagnetic/paramagnetic behaviour?

(i) \(\mathrm{N_2 \rightarrow N_2^+ + e^-}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{O_2 \rightarrow O_2^+ + e^-}\)
(iii) \(\mathrm{O_2 + e^- \rightarrow O_2^-}\)

What is the value of \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^0})\)?

[The standard reduction potential values are \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}) = 0.77\ \mathrm{V}\), and \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}/Fe^0}) = -0.44\ \mathrm{V}\)]

rows.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
rows.text: What are the correct orders of stability for the following compounds?

Consider the following reaction scheme:

\(\mathrm{CrCl_3\cdot 6H_2O}\) (**P**) \(\xrightarrow{\text{concentrated } \mathrm{NH_3} \text{ solution (excess)}}\) **Q**

**P** \(\xrightarrow{\text{excess } \mathrm{AgNO_3}}\) 1 mole AgCl precipitated per mole of **P**

**Q** \(\xrightarrow{\text{excess } \mathrm{AgNO_3}}\) 3 moles AgCl precipitated per mole of **Q**

Which among the following statements is correct?
options: **P** shows geometrical isomerism and absorbs light of higher wavelength than that of **Q**.
Both **P** and **Q** show geometrical isomerism and **P** absorbs light of higher wavelength than that of **Q**.
**Q** shows geometrical isomerism and absorbs light of higher wavelength than that of **P**.
**P** shows geometrical isomerism and absorbs light of lower wavelength than that of **Q**.
rows._flag: The scheme is printed as a diagram (P across to Q with the reagent over the arrow, and a down arrow from each to its AgCl result); typed here as three lines with the same words.

rows.text:
What are the major products formed in the following reaction sequence?

\(\mathrm{PhCH{=}C(CH_3)CH_2CH_3} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(iii)\ PhMgBr\ (excess\ of\ 2\ equivalents);\ (iv)\ H_3O^+}]{\mathrm{(i)\ O_3;\ (ii)\ Zn\ dust,\ H_2O}}\)
rows._flag: Starting alkene is drawn as a skeletal structure (Ph on one alkene carbon, CH3 and CH2CH3 on the other), typed here as a condensed formula; the drawing's geometry is not carried. Option 2's ketone chain length could not be read with certainty from the drawing, so it is described.

rows.text:
What is the major product in the reaction sequence given below?

\(\mathrm{Ph(CH_2)_3CN} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ H_2O;\ (iii)\ Zn\text{-}Hg/conc.\ HCl}]{\mathrm{(i)\ DIBAL\text{-}H\ (1\ equivalent)}}\)

figure.note: Skeletal structure Ph-(zig-zag chain)-CN, then an arrow with reagents (i) DIBAL-H (1 equivalent), (ii) H2O above it and (iii) Zn-Hg/conc. HCl below it.

rows.text: Compound **I** undergoes hydroboration-oxidation reaction with \(\mathrm{(BH_3)_2}\) followed by treatment with \(\mathrm{H_2O_2}\) and aqueous NaOH to produce another compound **II**, which upon oxidation with \(\mathrm{CrO_3}\) gives 2,3-dimethyl-cyclohexanone as the product. What is the structure of **I**?

The work done when one mole of an ideal gas expands at constant temperature \(T\) from volume \(V\) to \(2V\) (in two equal steps of volume in a linear fashion) is \(\frac{7}{12}\mathrm{R}T\). How much more work would be done by the gas if it expands in three equal steps?
[R is the universal gas constant]

At a particular temperature, the magnitude of the rate constant of a reaction is \(5 \times 10^{-5}\) and the unit of the pre-exponential factor of the Arrhenius equation for this reaction is \(\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}\,min^{-1}}\). Which of the following plots is correct for this reaction?

[Note: \([\mathrm{R}]_0\) is the initial concentration and \(t_{1/2}\) is the half-life of the reaction]
options: Plot of \(t_{1/2}\) against \([\mathrm{R}]_0\): a straight line rising from near the origin
Plot of \(t_{1/2}\) against \([\mathrm{R}]_0\): a horizontal straight line
Plot of \(t_{1/2}\) against \([\mathrm{R}]_0\): a curve rising ever more steeply
Plot of \(t_{1/2}\) against \([\mathrm{R}]_0\): a straight line falling

rows.text:
What is the time period of revolution of an electron in the fourth Bohr orbit of \(\mathrm{He^+}\)?

[Bohr radius \(= 52.9\) picometers, mass of an electron \(= 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}\), Planck's constant \(= 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{Js}\)]

The dipole moments of three \(\mathrm{AB_3}\)-type molecules **I**, **II**, and **III** are measured to be 0.0 D, 0.2 D, and 1.5 D, respectively. Which one of the following options is correct regarding the identity of **I**, **II**, and **III**?

During the charging and discharging of a lead-acid battery (a Pb anode, a grid of Pb packed with \(\mathrm{PbO_2}\) as cathode, and an aqueous solution of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) as an electrolyte), which of the following redox reactions does NOT occur?
